title: Higher-Dimensional Boundary Measure of Polynomial Sublevel Sets

problemStatement.formal: \inf_{f \in \mathbb{C}[z_1,\dots,z_d]} \Lambda_d(f) = c_d > 0, \text{ with } c_1 = 2, \text{ where } \Lambda_d(f) = \max_C \sigma_{2d-1}(\partial C) \text{ over bounded components } C \text{ of } \{|f| < 1\}, \text{ roots in } \overline{\mathbb{D}}^d; \text{ the infimum is not attained and is approached by } \prod_j (z_j^n - 1) \text{ as } n \to \infty.
problemStatement.plain: Tang's theorem says that in one complex variable, the shortest possible boundary length of a component of {|f| < 1} (over polynomials with roots in the unit disk) is exactly 2, approached but never attained. This problem asks the analogous question in several complex variables: for f(z_1,...,z_d), the sublevel set {|f| < 1} lives in C^d and its boundary is a real hypersurface of dimension 2d-1. Measuring boundary size by (2d-1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure, we conjecture the infimum over such polynomials is a positive dimensional constant c_d, not attained, and approached by tensor products of the extremal one-variable polynomials.
whyMatters: Tests whether the sharp, unattained one-variable extremal phenomenon of Tang's theorem survives in higher dimensions, where sublevel-set geometry is far richer.

Polynomial sublevel sets and their boundaries are central objects in pluripotential theory, where log|f| is plurisubharmonic; sharp metric bounds connect to Bernstein-Markov measures, capacities of pluripolar sets, and the Bernstein-Walsh inequality.
Even establishing existence and positivity of the dimensional constant c_d would give the first genuinely multivariate analogue of Tang's result.

proven: Tang's theorem (one variable): inf_f Lambda_1(f) = 2, not attained, approached by z^n - 1 (Proc. AMS 2021, doi:10.1090/proc/15470); formalized in this gallery as erdos-1044 via the axiom tang_infimum_eq_two.
Erdos-Herzog-Piranian (1958) introduced Lambda(f) and the level-set metric program.
Pluripotential foundations (Klimek 1991): {|f| < 1} = {log|f| < 0} governed by the plurisubharmonic potential log|f|; boundary contained in the real-analytic set {|f|^2 = 1}.
Federer's coarea formula and rectifiable-set theory provide the machinery to define the (2d-1)-Hausdorff boundary measure rigorously.
open: The exact or even approximate value of c_d for any d >= 2.
Whether the infimum is finite and strictly positive at all in dimension d >= 2 (existence/positivity of c_d).
Whether the tensor-product family prod_j (z_j^n - 1) actually realizes the infimum in the limit.
Whether the 'not attained' phenomenon persists in higher dimensions.
knownResults.goal: Formalize a precise statement of the several-variable conjecture and prove the tractable structural pieces: (1) define the sublevel set and axiomatize the (2d-1)-Hausdorff boundary functional Lambda_d, mirroring the parent's maxBoundaryLength; (2) prove the compatibility/reduction lemma recovering Tang's constant 2 on one-variable slices/products; (3) state higher_dim_infimum_positive as an axiom with the d=1 specialization proved equal to Tang's statement.
